help.title: How to use Chess Trainer
help.intro: Chess Trainer is for practice: drill your openings against a bot that plays your lines, keep playing against Stockfish when theory ends, and review your games. Everything runs and stays on your computer.
help.fairPlay.title: Never use it to cheat
help.fairPlay.text: Do not use Chess Trainer, or any engine, during a game against another person, online or over the board. That is cheating, and Lichess, Chess.com and FIDE ban it. Train before and after your games, never during them.
help.eval.title: The evaluation here is basic
help.eval.text: The evaluation bar and the move icons (best move, mistake, blunder…) come from a quick Stockfish check and are only a hint. For a real analysis, export the PGN and analyse it on Lichess, Chess.com or another analysis tool.
help.start.title: Start a game
help.start.opening: Opening: pick your color and tick the openings and variations to drill. Each ticked variation has the same chance of being drawn. Playing a move from a variation you did not tick counts as leaving theory.
help.start.saved: Saved game: train the line of a game you played or imported, so its moves are checked, or play on from any of its positions.
help.start.chess960: Chess960: roll a starting position or paste the FEN of one of the 960. To castle, click the king and then a square between it and the rook, or the rook itself.
help.start.level: Bot level: the rating beside each level is nominal, on Stockfish's own scale, and has not been measured. It is not a Lichess or Chess.com rating.
help.start.time: Time control: the presets of a real tournament clock, from bullet to classical, or no clock. The bot's response time is Human, which spends its clock like a person, or Instant.
help.start.options: Options: warn when you leave theory, allow premoves, and let the bot deviate from its line on purpose, from a chosen move, so you also train against surprises.
help.play.title: During the game
help.play.moves: Click or drag the pieces. The bot plays the book moves of the drawn line, and when theory ends, or someone leaves it, Stockfish takes over at the chosen level.
help.play.chips: The chips under the board say whose move it is, whether you are still in theory, and where you or the bot left it.
help.play.showMoves: Show moves, in the right bar, hides the opening name and the move list until the end of the game: play without hints, or write the moves on paper.
help.play.premoves: With premoves on, you can queue one move while the bot thinks. With premoves off, Take back undoes your last move while the bot's reply is not shown yet.
help.play.resign: Resign asks for a second click, so a stray click does not end the game.
help.end.title: After the game
help.end.card: The card under the move list shows the result, the variation, how far theory went, and each deviation with the expected move.
help.end.pgn: Copy or download the PGN. New Game starts the next one with the same choices.
help.paper.title: Train like an official game
help.paper.print: Open Scoresheet in the menu and print it, or save it as a PDF.
help.paper.setup: Choose a long time control, such as rapid or classical, and untick Show moves.
help.paper.write: Write every move, yours and the bot's, right after it is played, as over the board. Fill in the header, the result and the signatures, to get used to a real tournament.
help.paper.compare: At the end, compare your sheet with the move list and the PGN, and look for the moves you wrote wrong.
help.review.title: Saved games and review
help.review.list: Every game is saved. Search and filter the list, open a game on the board and go through it with the buttons or the arrow keys, Home and End.
help.review.play: Play from here starts a new game from the position on the board.
help.review.export: Tick games to export them as PGN or to delete them.
help.openings.title: Openings
help.openings.browse: Go through every line of the book on the board, and tick lines to export them as PGN.
help.import.title: Import games
help.import.sources: Bring your games from Chess.com or Lichess by username and period, or paste or upload a PGN. They go to Saved games, ready to review or to train.
help.analyse.title: Analyse elsewhere
help.analyse.export: Get the PGN from the end-of-game card or from Saved games.
help.analyse.paste: On Lichess or Chess.com, open the analysis board and paste or import the PGN, for a full analysis by a stronger setup.
